issues.legal_issue: Failure to object promptly to the mode of proving an otherwise admissible document waives a later challenge to that mode of proof.
material_facts: The plaintiff tendered a certified copy of a registered sale deed as evidence, and it was marked and admitted without objection.
The defendant’s later objection concerned the mode of proving the deed, rather than whether the deed was itself admissible in evidence.
The original deed was available in collateral proceedings and could have been produced if an objection had been made at trial.
The defendant first challenged the sufficiency of the mode of proof in the lower appellate court.
issues.conclusion: The defendant could not raise the mode-of-proof objection for the first time in the lower appellate court; the civil appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: An objection that an otherwise admissible document was proved by an irregular or insufficient mode must be raised when the document is tendered and before it is marked as an exhibit. If a timely objection could have allowed the party tendering the document to cure the defect, failure to object waives the objection. The Court applied Order XIII Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure and relied on R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Arulmigu Viswesaraswami & V.P. Temple, Gopal Das & Anr. v. Sri Thakurji & Ors., and the statement in Sarkar on Evidence. The asserted need to lay a foundation for secondary evidence under Section 65(a) and (f) of the Evidence Act did not preserve a belated objection to the mode of proof; the Court did not decide the appeal by independently resolving the applicability of Section 90 of that Act.

rule.if: civil_evidence_dispute and document_is_otherwise_admissible and objection_concerns_mode_of_proof and document_marked_without_timely_objection and objection_first_raised_on_appeal and timely_objection_could_enable_cure

predicates.civil_evidence_dispute: The dispute is a civil proceeding in which a party relies on documentary evidence.
predicates.document_is_otherwise_admissible: The document is not challenged as inherently inadmissible in evidence.
predicates.objection_concerns_mode_of_proof: The opposing party disputes the method used to prove the document, rather than its inherent admissibility.
predicates.document_marked_without_timely_objection: The document is admitted and marked as an exhibit without an objection when it is tendered.
predicates.objection_first_raised_on_appeal: The opposing party first raises the mode-of-proof objection at an appellate stage.
predicates.timely_objection_could_enable_cure: An objection made when the document was tendered could have allowed the party relying on it to use a proper method of proof.

issues.definition: When an otherwise admissible document is admitted without a timely mode-of-proof objection, and an objection at the proper time could have enabled the relying party to cure the proof, a challenge to that mode raised only on appeal is waived.
